#### Clase `MaskedRecords` (Línea 76)
- **Docstring:** _Attributes
----------
_data : recarray
    Underlying data, as a record array.
_mask : boolean array
    Mask of the records. A record is masked when all its fields are
    masked.
_fieldmask : boolean recarray
    Record array of booleans, setting the mask of each individual field
    of each record.
_fill_value : record
    Filling values for each field._
- **Métodos:**
  - `def __new__(cls, shape, dtype, buf, offset, strides, formats, names, titles, byteorder, aligned, mask, hard_mask, fill_value, keep_mask, copy)` (Línea 94): Sin docstring.
  - `def __array_finalize__(self, obj)` (Línea 134): Sin docstring.
  - `def _data(self)` (Línea 154): Returns the data as a recarray.

  - `def __getattribute__(self, attr)` (Línea 180): Sin docstring.
  - `def __setattr__(self, attr, val)` (Línea 227): Sets the attribute attr to the value val.
  - `def __getitem__(self, indx)` (Línea 283): Returns all the fields sharing the same fieldname base.

The fieldname base is either `_data` or `_mask`.
  - `def __setitem__(self, indx, value)` (Línea 315): Sets the given record to value.
  - `def __str__(self)` (Línea 324): Calculates the string representation.
  - `def __repr__(self)` (Línea 338): Calculates the repr representation.
  - `def view(self, dtype, type)` (Línea 351): Returns a view of the mrecarray.
  - `def harden_mask(self)` (Línea 368): Forces the mask to hard.
  - `def soften_mask(self)` (Línea 375): Forces the mask to soft
  - `def copy(self)` (Línea 382): Returns a copy of the masked record.
  - `def tolist(self, fill_value)` (Línea 391): Return the data portion of the array as a list.

Data items are converted to the nearest compatible Python type.
Masked values are converted to fill_value. If fill_value is None,
the corresponding entries in the output list will be ``None``.
  - `def __getstate__(self)` (Línea 407): Return the internal state of the masked array.

This is for pickling.
  - `def __setstate__(self, state)` (Línea 423): Restore the internal state of the masked array.

This is for pickling.  ``state`` is typically the output of the
``__getstate__`` output, and is a 5-tuple:

- class name
- a tuple giving the shape of the data
- a typecode for the data
- a binary string for the data
- a binary string for the mask.
  - `def __reduce__(self)` (Línea 443): Return a 3-tuple for pickling a MaskedArray.

#### `def fromarrays(arraylist, dtype, shape, formats, names, titles, aligned, byteorder, fill_value)` (Línea 471)
- **Propósito:** Creates a mrecarray from a (flat) list of masked arrays.

Parameters
----------
arraylist : sequence
    A list of (masked) arrays. Each element of the sequence is first converted
    to a masked array if needed. If a 2D array is passed as argument, it is
    processed line by line
dtype : {None, dtype}, optional
    Data type descriptor.
shape : {None, integer}, optional
    Number of records. If None, shape is defined from the shape of the
    first array in the list.
formats : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of formats for each individual field. If None, the formats will
    be autodetected by inspecting the fields and selecting the highest dtype
    possible.
names : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of the names of each field.
fill_value : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of data to be used as filling values.

Notes
-----
Lists of tuples should be preferred over lists of lists for faster processing.
- **Firma:** `def fromarrays(arraylist, dtype, shape, formats, names, titles, aligned, byteorder, fill_value)`
- **Retorno / Efectos:** Consulta código fuente.

#### `def fromrecords(reclist, dtype, shape, formats, names, titles, aligned, byteorder, fill_value, mask)` (Línea 514)
- **Propósito:** Creates a MaskedRecords from a list of records.

Parameters
----------
reclist : sequence
    A list of records. Each element of the sequence is first converted
    to a masked array if needed. If a 2D array is passed as argument, it is
    processed line by line
dtype : {None, dtype}, optional
    Data type descriptor.
shape : {None,int}, optional
    Number of records. If None, ``shape`` is defined from the shape of the
    first array in the list.
formats : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of formats for each individual field. If None, the formats will
    be autodetected by inspecting the fields and selecting the highest dtype
    possible.
names : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of the names of each field.
fill_value : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of data to be used as filling values.
mask : {nomask, sequence}, optional.
    External mask to apply on the data.

Notes
-----
Lists of tuples should be preferred over lists of lists for faster processing.
- **Firma:** `def fromrecords(reclist, dtype, shape, formats, names, titles, aligned, byteorder, fill_value, mask)`

#### `def _guessvartypes(arr)` (Línea 579)
- **Propósito:** Tries to guess the dtypes of the str_ ndarray `arr`.

Guesses by testing element-wise conversion. Returns a list of dtypes.
The array is first converted to ndarray. If the array is 2D, the test
is performed on the first line. An exception is raised if the file is
3D or more.
- **Firma:** `def _guessvartypes(arr)`

#### `def fromtextfile(fname, delimiter, commentchar, missingchar, varnames, vartypes)` (Línea 636)
- **Propósito:** Creates a mrecarray from data stored in the file `filename`.

Parameters
----------
fname : {file name/handle}
    Handle of an opened file.
delimiter : {None, string}, optional
    Alphanumeric character used to separate columns in the file.
    If None, any (group of) white spacestring(s) will be used.
commentchar : {'#', string}, optional
    Alphanumeric character used to mark the start of a comment.
missingchar : {'', string}, optional
    String indicating missing data, and used to create the masks.
varnames : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of the variable names. If None, a list will be created from
    the first non empty line of the file.
vartypes : {None, sequence}, optional
    Sequence of the variables dtypes. If None, it will be estimated from
    the first non-commented line.


Ultra simple: the varnames are in the header, one line
- **Firma:** `def fromtextfile(fname, delimiter, commentchar, missingchar, varnames, vartypes)`
- **Retorno / Efectos:** Consulta código fuente.

#### `def addfield(mrecord, newfield, newfieldname)` (Línea 705)
- **Propósito:** Adds a new field to the masked record array

Uses `newfield` as data and `newfieldname` as name. If `newfieldname`
is None, the new field name is set to 'fi', where `i` is the number of
existing fields.
